questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was a city that seemed safe and a country that had everything under control. It seems that some of the more southern universities are more "relaxed" about specific dates. Thought it was lovely that GU seemed so organized and offered interesting courses. It is also very close to Finland and Norway so a lot of winter experiences!

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Gothenburg is not necessarily a destination a lot of people choose. But that is really lovely because then you will meet many different people from many different countries and not just rely on danes. Also got several swedish friends!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy! I know some experienced some small problems but I had none. Everything from courses, dates, activities was accessible and easy to attend.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were several social activities and the school had 3 introduction days. Including ESN that hosted a lot of activities.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Very lovely experience. Everybody was very including and sweet!

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: A had a friend before going where i could move in. But several just received accommodation from GU. Those were really social and fun to stay at as well. Otherwise facebook is also a good way to find housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: They don't really bicycle her because of the hills. So swedes highly depend on the tram which is romantic but not always to fast. Therefor living an hour from campus would be annoying on long term.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: No

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: See reason beneath.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It is a very different system as Sweden does "pace". This means that most often you will only have one course at a time if it has a pace on 100%. I had to 15 points courses both on 100% pace meaning a had one from september-november and then a course from november-january. So you do the exams during the semester. This also means a lot of courses can't be combined as they have to be in different periods of the semester or have the same pace fx both on 50% meaning in total 100%.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always ask the administration and they had really good examples to help. But it was difficult to find combined courses as a lot where on the same time. So i had to compromise with my choices to make it work.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: In the end i got just what i wanted but i also only had 3 possible combinations of courses so i would be satisfied no matter the outcome.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look at the paces and times of the semester! This makes it immediately clear which subjects you can combine so you don't fall in love with two courses in the same period.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was very satisfied with one and the other was the first time that it was enrolled so it was just less organized.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was very similar to the danish level. But because you only have one course at a time i only went to school 1-2 times at the most 3 times a week. I had a lot of readings and home written papers though which was more demanding during the semester but then less during the exam period. They also have mandatory seminars which also required more preparation.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very similar traditional lectures with the same breaks and meeting hours. Some of the teachers have also worked at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Global gender studies and Human rights in policy and practice

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Especially Human rights in policy and practice! Learned so much from that course especially in this time in the world. I already had gender studies before this course but a lot of topics were still new or elaborated so i would also recommend this.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: See next.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All museums are free for students and the both GU and ESN hosted athletic events and clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Both the university and ESN hosted a lot but it was very popular so you had to be very fast. Otherwise the city is very easy to manage and get around. A lot of small ferry busses go to the island outside the city! You can also play ping pong for free at slice every tuesday. A lot of small but really funny stuff! You can also go to Oslo or Stockholm. And please visit all the lovely second hand stores.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Islands, Oslo, Stockholm visit other friends in europe! Go on the ESn trips. Party, go to funny bars and FIKA!!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy as a dane. You don't have to speak english at cafes or when shopping. The Culture is also basically the same.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Often there are also swedes in your course. I gained swedish friends that way. Otherwise dare to engage with others when going on bars or cafes. But class is definitely easiest.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not many, maybe that they don't really bicycle. Also that pretty much can't smoke anywhere but since i don't it was just nice. Also systembolaget where you buy alcohol is closed after 15 on saturdays so always have some beers or wine at home.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Fika again, just love how they always prioritise coziness. Also how polite they are was really lovely.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Really go through the courses and see if they match in time and pace 
2. They really want you to pass so don't feel to strongly about failing or missing assignments
3. Enjoy all the lovely cafes, libraries and school facilities

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have an international bank account as Revolut as it allows free international payment. The app is exactly like mobilepay.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: That europe all of a sudden seemed very small and that i am so thankful for my international friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It is scary to study at another school you don't know the expectations and level. But you truly develop from a challenge. Even though everything was new in different in the beginning it ended up being the most relaxed and beautiful time through my whole university experience.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go to GU and have fun!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
